general.name: Developer Documentation
general.description: Welcome to the Torio Client developer documentation. This section covers the internal memory architecture, scanning routines, and injection frameworks used in the WPF client.
general.content:
where the code lives, and what to expect from it.

- the current client is written in c# / wpf. the v2 source is not published yet, it unlocks once a stable version ships
- the python prototype, up to v1.1.0-beta.3, is public at [kukentyan/torio-master](https://github.com/kukentyan/torio-master)
- releases go out through the [github releases page](https://github.com/Uncle-Awrt/Torio-Client/releases), beta tags first

**support policy**: if something breaks, do not open a github issue. the [discord](https://discord.gg/xq8sWQhuXG) is the only support channel, issues opened on the repo get closed unanswered.

general.name: Memory Scanner Architecture
general.description: The core subsystem responsible for reading and analyzing the game process memory. It detects game state changes such as World Entry/Exit and Menu states by scanning for specific Array of Bytes (AOB) signatures.
general.content:
the part everything else stands on.

on connect, the client:

1. finds the running bedrock process
2. reads the game version and picks the matching offset set
3. scans memory for the local player, entities and world state
4. feeds a live view of that data to every active module

modules never talk to the game directly, they read from this layer. that is also why an unsupported game version stops you at the connect screen instead of crashing mid-match. offsets are per-version and get updated with each new bedrock release.

visual.name: Ambience / Weather Changer
visual.description: Customizes client-side skybox lighting, weather states, and rain opacity.
visual.content: provides full client-side control over world weather and ambient lighting. force clear skies, toggle rain and thunderstorms, or adjust weather opacity and custom time ticks independent of server weather.

visual.name: Anti Blindness
visual.description: Disables blindness, darkness, and nausea visual distortion shaders completely.
visual.content: patches the post-processing screen shader flags in memory, completely eliminating darkness, blindness, and nausea effect overlays for crystal clear visibility in deep dark caves and PvP battles.

visual.name: Behind You (Rear View)
visual.description: Projects a tactical rear-view camera mirror to monitor enemies approaching from behind.
visual.content: renders an inverted perspective mirror or rear-threat radar on the screen, letting you watch your back and anticipate flanking players in combat without manually turning your camera around.

visual.name: Block / Storage ESP
visual.description: Highlights valuable ores, chests, shulker boxes, and containers through walls.
visual.content: renders distinct 3D wireframe boxes through solid terrain around target blocks, including diamond ores, ancient debris, normal chests, trapped chests, ender chests, and shulkers with configurable colors.

visual.name: China Hat
visual.description: Renders a smooth 3D cosmetic conical hat over your character in third-person view.
visual.content: draws a customizable 3D conical hat visual directly above your player model with adjustable radius, height, color gradients, and opacity in third-person camera mode.

visual.name: ESP
visual.description: Draws 2D bounding boxes and health bars around other players through walls.
visual.content: 2d bounding boxes drawn around entities, visible straight through walls. boxes come with health bars, so you can read a fight before committing to it. range and colors are configurable in settings.

visual.name: Fake Lag Visual (Ghost Box)
visual.description: Renders a bounding box at your server-side position while FakeLag or Blink is active.
visual.content: displays a visual 3D ghost box indicating the exact coordinate position where the server and other players currently perceive your player model while packet choking or lag simulation is enabled.

visual.name: Force Show Coordinates
visual.description: Enables coordinate HUD display by rewriting local player settings state in memory.
visual.content: flips the game's own coordinate hud on, even on servers that hide it. it works by rewriting the local player setting, so the server is never asked and never knows.

visual.name: Fullbright
visual.description: Instantly increases game brightness to maximum level, removing dark areas and shadows.
visual.content: zero to full light, everywhere, permanently. caves, night, the void, all lit. brightness is forced client-side, so torches become a style choice.

visual.name: Hide and Seek Helper
visual.description: Highlights disguised players and block props in hide-and-seek minigames.
visual.content: identifies player entities disguised as blocks or props in minigames and renders bounding box highlights and distance tags over them, making hidden players easily identifiable.

visual.name: Hit Particles
visual.description: Spawns custom client-side visual particle bursts upon striking enemies.
visual.content: generates customizable particle bursts (hearts, stars, smoke, crit sparks) around target entities whenever you deal damage, enhancing hit feedback.

visual.name: Media Overlay
visual.description: Displays currently playing music tracks and playback status in a clean HUD widget.
visual.content: integrates with the Windows System Media Transport Controls API to show your currently playing song title, artist name, and playback progress bar directly on the client overlay.

visual.name: Name Tags
visual.description: Draws clear, unscaled nameplates showing health, distance, and gear through walls.
visual.content: replaces standard entity nameplates with high-visibility billboard tags rendered at uniform size regardless of distance, showing player names, current health numbers, and active equipment through solid blocks.

visual.name: Player Trail
visual.description: Draws a smooth glowing particle or ribbon trail behind your movement path.
visual.content: records player position history and draws a sleek, customizable ribbon or trail behind your character as you run, jump, or fall.

visual.name: Time Changer
visual.description: Changes client-side game time to any hour of the day.
visual.content: sets the client-side clock to any hour you want. the server keeps its own time, you simply see the lighting you prefer. useful for recording and for seeing what you are doing at night.

visual.name: Tracers
visual.description: Draws directional indicator lines from your crosshair or feet to nearby players.
visual.content: projects 2D or 3D vector lines connecting your screen center or player feet directly to target entities, allowing effortless tracking of opponents in complex terrain or fast-paced PvP.

visual.name: True Sight
visual.description: Reveals invisible entities (like players under invisibility potion status or spectating admins).
visual.content: drops the invisibility flag client-side. invisible players, mobs and effects all render normally on your screen, while everyone else sees nothing at all.

visual.name: Zoom
visual.description: Adjusts camera Field of View (FOV) state dynamically, acting as a tactical telescope.
visual.content: a camera fov toggle acting as a scope. hold or toggle the bind, and set the zoom level in settings. good for spotting players across a render distance.

combat.name: Aim Assist
combat.description: Smoothly guides your crosshair towards nearby players to improve target tracking and landing hits.
combat.content: guides your crosshair toward nearby players. only players are tracked, mobs and animals are ignored on purpose. yaw and pitch corrections use dynamic values, so the pull stays smooth instead of jittery.

combat.name: Auto Clicker
combat.description: Automates clicking at high rates for both left and right mouse buttons.
combat.content:
left and right click automation with randomizer support, so every interval lands inside believable human ranges.

- **menu check** pauses it while any gui is open
- **block break check** pauses it while you are mining

both checks are individual toggles, pick the combination that fits how you play.

combat.name: Auto Crystal
combat.description: Automatically places and detonates End Crystals at high speeds for competitive PvP.
combat.content: scans surrounding targets and automatically handles the placement and immediate detonation of end crystals in crystal PvP fights. includes configurable placement delays, break delays, and hit rate limits to ensure reliable detonation without desync.

combat.name: Auto Mace
combat.description: Automatically swaps to a Mace mid-air right before landing a downward smash attack.
combat.content: detects when the local player is falling from sufficient height and automatically swaps to a mace immediately before landing a hit to deliver a lethal smash attack, then instantly reverts back to your previous hotbar slot.

combat.name: Back Track
combat.description: Delays player position updates, allowing you to hit their past positions (ticks backtrack).
combat.content:
delays incoming player positions through a smooth continuous queue, so enemies appear where they were moments ago and you can hit the ghost of them.

- **flow** mode toggles on and off
- **hold** mode stays active while you hold the bind

combat.name: Double Clicker
combat.description: Injects secondary mouse clicks on left-button triggers to increase PVP click-rates.
combat.content: fires a second click on every real left click you make, effectively doubling your cps without touching any click speed settings. nothing to configure beyond the toggle.

combat.name: Fake Lag
combat.description: Delays outgoing network packets to simulate high ping, throwing off opponents tracking.
combat.content:
delays your own outgoing movement packets, so you stutter and lag on other players' screens while your game stays completely smooth.

- **flow** and **hold** modes like backtrack
- **hardstop on hit** snaps you back the moment you take or land a hit

previously called reverse backtrack.

combat.name: Ghost Hand
combat.description: Interact with chests, containers, and blocks through solid walls and entities.
combat.content: bypasses line-of-sight raycast restrictions for block interactions, allowing you to open chests, furnaces, hoppers, or use utility blocks through walls and obstructing players without moving out of cover.

combat.name: Hitbox
combat.description: Expands the physical size of enemy hitboxes in memory, allowing you to land attacks from wider angles.
combat.content: expands entity hitboxes in memory. bigger boxes mean easier tracking and more forgiving swings. the world looks exactly the same, the targets are just easier to land hits on.

combat.name: Pearl Aimbot
combat.description: Calculates ballistic projectile trajectories and aims Ender Pearls with pinpoint accuracy.
combat.content: uses physical projectile simulation algorithms to automatically adjust your pitch and yaw angles when throwing ender pearls, ensuring accurate landing at target coordinates, escape positions, or enemy locations.

combat.name: Reach
combat.description: Extends your maximum attack range in memory, allowing you to strike players from further away.
combat.content: extends your melee attack distance past the vanilla limit. randomizer support keeps the extension inside believable bounds instead of a flat number every swing.

combat.name: Sticky Aim
combat.description: Locks your crosshair rotation tracking to the closest player hitbox in range.
combat.content: fine-tunes your sensitivity while you are manually aiming at someone, so your crosshair sticks to the target instead of sliding past it. it only kicks in while you are already aiming, never pulls on its own. previously called micro aim.

combat.name: Trigger Bot
combat.description: Automatically triggers an attack the exact millisecond your crosshair passes over an enemy entity.
combat.content:
swings the instant your crosshair sits on a target. three modes:

- **first hit** fires once per approach
- **auto click** keeps swinging while the target stays under your crosshair
- **hitselect** only activates while you are being hit and already aiming back at the attacker

movement.name: Air Acceleration
movement.description: Enhances horizontal strafe control and air speed when jumping.
movement.content: changes how fast you accelerate mid-air, so strafing during jumps actually shifts your momentum. randomizer support included, keep it subtle or go loud.

movement.name: Air Jump
movement.description: Allows continuous jumping while airborne as if standing on solid ground.
movement.content: resets the on-ground state in local player memory while falling or airborne, enabling you to jump repeatedly mid-air to scale steep terrain or traverse gaps without placing blocks.

movement.name: Auto Block Reset
movement.description: Instantly places a block beneath your feet when damaged to cancel knockback momentum.
movement.content: monitors incoming player damage events and automatically aims down to place a block beneath your feet, instantly canceling horizontal knockback momentum before restoring your crosshair back to your target.

movement.name: Auto S-Tap
movement.description: Sends automated backward movement pulses upon landing a hit to maintain combo spacing.
movement.content: automatically releases forward movement and taps the backward key (S) for a few milliseconds immediately after striking an opponent, helping you maintain optimal hit spacing and deal continuous combo knockback.

movement.name: Jump Reset
movement.description: Simulates high-velocity downward momentum the moment you take damage, resetting your knockback instantly.
movement.content: fires a jump the exact moment you take damage in combat, automating the jump reset timing used to cut knockback combos. no timing practice required.

movement.name: Lag Switch
movement.description: Manually toggles packet transmission updates to simulate sudden server latency spikes.
movement.content: hold the bind to freeze outgoing packets and fake a connection spike. everything you do queues up, and releases the moment you let go. short taps for quick desyncs, long holds for real chaos.

movement.name: No Jump Delay
movement.description: Removes the 10-tick jump cooldown, allowing instant and consecutive bunny hops.
movement.content: continuously clears the internal jump cooldown counter in game memory, letting you jump on the exact tick you touch the ground for smoother, faster bunny hops and momentum maintenance.

movement.name: No Slowdown
movement.description: Maintains 100% full movement speed while eating, charging bows, or walking in webs.
movement.content: hooks the player speed reduction routine in memory to prevent the slowdown penalty normally applied while consuming food, drinking potions, using shields, drawing bows, or traversing cobwebs.

movement.name: Sprint
movement.description: Forces your player entity to maintain sprinting speed in all directions.
movement.content: sprint without holding the key. forced in every direction, including backwards and sideways. your pinky will thank you.

movement.name: Timer
movement.description: Speeds up or slows down the game tick rate client-side.
movement.content: speeds up or slows down the client tick rate, so the game runs faster or slower than the server expects. randomizer support keeps the rate moving instead of pinned.

movement.name: Velocity
movement.description: Scales the knockback velocity received from attacks and environmental hazards.
movement.content: scales incoming knockback with separate **horizontal (x/z)** and **vertical (y)** multipliers. dial it from reduced to zero, or mix and match to keep some vertical pop while cutting horizontal push.

movement.name: W-Tap
movement.description: Automates sprint-resetting by micro-pausing forward movement on every hit.
movement.content: replicates the classic PvP w-tapping technique by releasing and re-engaging forward sprint immediately after an attack registers, maximizing the knockback dealt to your target on every consecutive hit.

utility.name: Array List
utility.description: Displays a real-time list of all active modules on your HUD.
utility.content: a live list of your enabled modules, rendered on the hud. what is on, at a glance. position and style are configurable, pair it with a clean theme and it doubles as a flex.

utility.name: Auto 360
utility.description: Triggers a rapid 360-degree spin of your camera with a single keybind.
utility.content: one bind, instant spin. supports **right**, **left** and **alternate** directions, with configurable sensitivity. the classic clip finisher.

utility.name: Auto Bow
utility.description: Automatically draws and releases bows at the perfect timing for maximum damage.
utility.content: charges the bow and releases at the right moment automatically. timing tracks the charge window, so every shot leaves at full power without you watching the meter.

utility.name: Auto Throw
utility.description: Throws projectiles (pearls, eggs, snowballs, potions) at rapid-fire speed.
utility.content: throws pearls, snowballs, eggs and splash potions on a bind. fire and forget, literally. works as a macro, so it throws whatever fits the moment.

utility.name: Blink
utility.description: Temporarily buffers outgoing movement packets to appear frozen before instantly teleporting.
utility.content: chokes and queues outgoing position and movement packets while allowing you to move freely client-side. upon disabling, all queued packets are dispatched simultaneously, making you appear to teleport across the map to other players.

utility.name: Custom Watermark
utility.description: Replaces the default overlay text with a customized client name and styling.
utility.content: your own text in the corner of the screen. font, size and content are all configurable. call the client whatever you want, we are not the police.

utility.name: Device ID Spoofer
utility.description: Randomizes unique hardware and device identifiers during server handshakes.
utility.content: intercepts client telemetry and login handshake packets to replace your persistent device ID, hardware UUID, and platform signatures with randomized values, preventing cross-session hardware-based tracking.

utility.name: Discord Rich Presence
utility.description: Displays customized Torio Client details on your Discord profile status.
utility.content: shows your current menu, server, game version and client status on your discord profile while you play. lets friends see exactly what you are running without asking.

utility.name: Duck Overlay
utility.description: Draws a cute animated duck mascot on your screen.
utility.content: an animated duck on your screen while you play. it does nothing. that is the entire point. if losing a fight to a sweater admin has you tilted, the duck is there for you.

utility.name: Fast Item
utility.description: Spams usage of items (like eating food or drinking potions) in a fraction of the normal time.
utility.content: cuts item use timers, so eating and drinking finish in a fraction of the normal time. pearls out faster, gaps down faster, fights survive longer.

utility.name: GUI Theme
utility.description: Customizes colors, glows, transparency, and style of the client overlay and menus.
utility.content: full accent color control with light and dark mode, plus glow and transparency settings. the entire look of the client is adjustable from gui settings, and there is a reset button for when you go too far.

utility.name: Reach Display Spoof
utility.description: Spoofs on-screen hit distance readouts in watermarks and HUDs for clean screen shares.
utility.content: clamps the reported hit reach distance in HUD indicators and on-screen overlays to a legit-looking maximum (e.g. 3.0 blocks), concealing expanded hitbox or reach values during screen shares or video recordings.

utility.name: Self Destruct
utility.description: Emergency unhooking system that restores vanilla memory and terminates the client cleanly.
utility.content: immediately unhooks all shellcode caves, restores original game instruction bytes, wipes runtime config memory, and cleanly closes the client process without leaving trace signatures or crashing the game.

utility.name: Stream Protect
utility.description: Hides all client HUD elements, overlays, and GUI windows from capture programs.
utility.content: hides client hud elements, overlays and gui windows from capture software. obs and discord screen shares see a clean game, your modules stay between you and the duck.

utility.name: System Tray
utility.description: Minimizes the WPF application into the Windows system tray instead of the taskbar.
utility.content: minimizes the client to the windows system tray instead of the taskbar. reopen from the tray icon whenever you need it, quit from there too.

core.name: Aim Detector
core.description: Captures and monitors target aiming states, updating crosshair alignment variables.
core.content: watches where the crosshair actually points and updates aim modules frame by frame, so triggerbot and sticky aim react to live positions instead of last tick's leftovers.

core.name: Block Break Detector
core.description: Monitors block mining state variables to dynamically pause click simulations when breaking structures.
core.content: tracks your mining state and pauses click automation while you break blocks. this is what keeps autoclicker from fighting your pickaxe mid-mine.

core.name: Local Player Coordinates
core.description: Monitors spatial parameters of the local player head to construct crosshair ray-casting lines.
core.content: reads the local player position every tick and hands it to whoever needs it. coordinate hud, aim math, movement modules, all of them read from here.

core.name: Menu Monitor
core.description: Monitors user menu states to pause active click features when settings or inventory containers are open.
core.content: watches for open guis and menus, in-game or in the client, and pauses click features while you are clicking through settings instead of playing.

core.name: Minecraft Process Monitor
core.description: Runs polling cycles checking process active handles to control startup hooks and memory scans.
core.content: polls for a running bedrock process and drives the connect flow: startup when the game appears, clean shutdown when it disappears. the connect screen leans on this one.

core.name: Minecraft Window Monitor
core.description: Tracks window focus and size alignments, synchronizing WPF overlay windows to game positions.
core.content: tracks the game window's focus, size and position, so the overlay gui stays glued to the right spot and external mode keeps its place when you alt-tab.

core.name: Player Damage Monitor
core.description: Monitors damage ticks to trigger Jump Reset knockback recovery loops.
core.content: watches damage ticks landing on you and triggers recovery logic at the right moment. jump reset runs on this feed.

core.name: Rotation & Angle Calculations
core.description: The mathematical trigonometry system responsible for computing targeted yaw and pitch angles relative to enemy entities.
core.content: the trig layer that turns world positions into yaw and pitch angles. aim assist, sticky aim and triggerbot all compute their corrections through it, which is why they agree with each other.

core.name: World Status Monitor
core.description: Monitors player session updates to set target context during world entries and exits.
core.content: tracks world and session state, so modules know when you are in a game, sitting in a menu or between servers, and behave accordingly instead of firing at the title screen.
